transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I can’t stop getting stuck on these awful ‘what if I missed something’ thoughts about my design files, and they’re taking over my workday. It feels like my brain just won't let me move on, and it's becoming completely exhausting.
Do you feel driven to perform certain behaviors or mental acts, like checking or rechecking things, in response to these thoughts?

Yes, I feel an overwhelming urge to do these repetitive checks just to ease the panic. I end up reopening the same files over and over—zooming in on text, counting my checks, and re-exporting artwork—until entire evenings disappear and I still don't feel safe sending them to the client.
Do these checking rituals follow specific rules or patterns, like needing to do them a certain number of times or in a particular way, even if it doesn’t make logical sense?

Yes, there's definitely a pattern—I feel forced to zoom in on every single line of text and count exactly how many times I've checked a page before I can even think about stopping. I'll also re-export the same artwork over and over in a specific sequence just to feel safe. It makes absolutely no logical sense and wastes hours of my time, but I feel completely trapped by these rules.
Do you feel that something bad will happen if you don't complete your checking rituals or follow the rules exactly?

Yes, absolutely. I get consumed by this intense panic that a tiny oversight, like a wrong color code, will slip through and completely ruin the client's business and my reputation. The checking is the only way I can try to quiet that dread, even though I still feel uneasy afterward.
